### Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Why | Alternative Rejected | Trade-off |
|----------|--------|-----|---------------------|-----------|
| "+N months" computation | Every effect via cumulative re-run of `shocks.runway` on lever-adjusted (income, spending, buffer, oneOff) | The judge formula is the single source of truth; a shortcut formula (e.g. `buffer/gap` deltas) can drift at the `no_shortfall`/cap branches | Direct formula on gap | One runway call per lever step; trivial cost (integer math, <1 ms budget) |
| Lever sizing base | Levers sized from **profile** numbers (S, F, P, insurance), never shocked ones | Judge hand-checks use part-1 metrics; shock additions (bills +15%, extra monthly) are not discretionary and must not be "cut away" by a lever | Size against shocked spending | Under a bills shock the trim lever cannot absorb the increase; that is the honest answer |
| Discretionary margin | `disc = max(0, S − (F + P))` with `trim_discretionary` spending down exactly to the F+P cut floor | Matches the E2-approved cut floor definition; zero when no margin exists (explicit "no margin" row) | Percent-of-spending cuts (arbitrary) | Accounts with tiny margins (68257: disc = $9.19) show +0.0 months; that is a true finding, not a bug |
| Levers below the floor | `defer_loan` (−P) and `shop_insurance` (−insurance) deliberately go under F+P and are labeled as structural moves ("simulated counterfactual") | Deferral is real bank hardship practice with P exact in the data; insurance renegotiation is bounded by `insurance_cents` | Forbidding all floor breaches (would kill 2 of 3 levers) | The printed floor line must say "ordinary cuts stop at F+P; labeled structural moves go under it on purpose" |
| Standing-orders lever | **REJECT** | `standing_orders.csv` is not in `profiles.json`; adding it means an E1 schema change (exact-key loader, verify.py, frozen fixtures) and the source is an undated snapshot | Precompute per-account order sums in E1 | Lever set misses "cancel discretionary standing orders"; acceptable, recorded in decisions |
| Secondary-buffer lever | **REJECT** | No cross-account linkage exists (transfers land at partner banks outside the dataset); `balance_series` is the same single account's money | "Restore buffer to 12-month peak" (not a lever the customer can pull) | `buffer_depleted` accounts show all levers at +0.0; surfaced as an honest plan line instead |
| Goal target | Keep `3 × S` starter with `6 × S` stretch chips (GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS = 6 = the EI duration) | Standard emergency-fund guidance is 3 to 6 months of spending; the challenge's own twist runs 6 months at 55%, so 3 is starter and 6 is storm-ready; both printed as "our definition" | 6 × S only (less reachable; weakens the goal story) or 3–6 range formula (two headline numbers) | A judge preferring 6 × S sees it as the stretch chip row |
| Months to target | Keep scaffold `ceil(target / contribution)` from zero (EXTEND verdict; keeps E2 invariant) + printed "savings on hand" disclosure line | Changing it breaks the approved E2 plan numbers and the invariant in the test plan | Netting B into months (see Q1) | Two facts on the card (months from zero, buffer on hand) instead of one netted number |
| Python twin | **RESTORE, test-side only** (no build.py/verify.py coupling) | Data Use rubric (25%) rewards "every plan number cross-checked by two independent implementations against frozen goldens"; cross-language drift is the recurring failure mode and `golden_fixtures.json` parity is the established remedy; drafts already exist so cost is ~150 lines | Abandon + delete (zero cost, loses the drift guard and the rubric argument) | Every future plan rule change needs two edits; a missed edit is a failing pytest, which is the point. Time-boxed fallback: abandon if the TS side slips (Q2) |
| Golden fixture file | New frozen `scripts/engine/golden_plans.json` (do not touch `golden_fixtures.json`) | `golden_fixtures.json` is frozen E1 hand computation; plans need their own frozen table with workings | Extend `golden_fixtures.json` | One more fixture file; matches the established pattern |
| ConsoleView/store | Zero changes; `buildPlanText` composes planMath internally | The one seam (`plan={derivation.plan}`) survives E3's concurrent mount work untouched; no merge conflicts | ConsoleView computes planMath in its useMemo and passes parts down | `buildPlanText` is a slightly larger composer; acceptable since it is already the "arithmetic lives here" layer |

### Interfaces

All money fields integer cents; all month counts integers; sentinels `MONTHS_UNREACHABLE = -1`, `CUT_NOT_APPLICABLE = -1` (existing).

```ts
// src/lib/planMath.ts (new)

/** The 6 month stretch cushion, the EI duration in the challenge twist. */
export const GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS = 6            // sits beside GOAL_TARGET_MONTHS = 3
export const GOAL_MILESTONE_MONTHS = [1, 2, 3, 6] as const

export interface GoalMilestone {
  monthsOfSpending: number        // k in "k months of typical spending"
  amountCents: number             // k x S, integer cents
  monthsToReach: number           // ceil(k x S / contribution), or MONTHS_UNREACHABLE
  isGoal: boolean                 // k === GOAL_TARGET_MONTHS
  isStretch: boolean              // k === GOAL_STRETCH_MONTHS
}
export function goalMilestones(incomeCents: number, spendingCents: number): GoalMilestone[]

export type LeverId = 'shop_insurance' | 'trim_discretionary' | 'defer_loan'

/** One lever's explicit effect on the shocked cash flow, integer cents. */
export interface LeverEffect {
  incomeDeltaCents: number        // 0 for every E4 lever
  spendingDeltaCents: number      // <= 0: every E4 lever cuts monthly spending
  bufferDeltaCents: number        // 0 for every E4 lever (no data backed buffer lever)
}

export interface Lever {
  id: LeverId
  label: string                   // plain words, the ladder row title
  caveat: string                  // honesty tag, "simulated counterfactual, ..." (dash clean)
  effect: LeverEffect
}

export interface LeverInputs {
  // Shocked numbers, straight from ShockResult (never re-derived here).
  shockedIncomeCents: number
  shockedSpendingCents: number
  oneOffCents: number
  bufferCents: number             // profile.buffer_cents (pre one-off), for the re-run
  // Profile numbers the levers are sized from (judge part-1 metrics).
  fixedCostsCents: number         // F
  loanPaymentCents: number        // P (0 when no running loan)
  insuranceCents: number          // median insurance
  typicalSpendingCents: number    // S
}

export interface LeverStep {
  lever: Lever
  incomeAfterCents: number        // cumulative, integer cents
  spendingAfterCents: number      // cumulative, integer cents
  bufferLeftCents: number         // bufferCents - oneOffCents (unchanged by E4 levers)
  runwayAfter: RunwayAnswer       // shocks.runway re-run from scratch after this step
  plusDeciMonths: number          // cumulative vs shocked baseline, tenths, >= 0
  stepDeciMonths: number          // marginal vs previous step, tenths, >= 0
}

export interface LeverLadder {
  baseline: RunwayAnswer          // the shocked runway each step improves on
  steps: LeverStep[]              // application order, only levers the data supports
}
export function leverLadder(input: LeverInputs): LeverLadder
```

**Lever semantics (the contract table):**

| Order | id | Availability | Effect (integer cents) | Honesty label (caveat) | Floor interaction |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `shop_insurance` | `insuranceCents > 0` | `spendingDelta = −insuranceCents` | "simulated counterfactual: premiums re-shopped, upper bound of renegotiation" | Goes under F+P on purpose (premium itself is renegotiated) |
| 2 | `trim_discretionary` | `disc = max(0, S − (F+P)) > 0` | `spendingDelta = −disc` | "simulated counterfactual: all discretionary spending above the fixed cost floor trimmed" | Lands exactly on F+P |
| 3 | `defer_loan` | `loanPaymentCents > 0` | `spendingDelta = −loanPaymentCents` | "simulated counterfactual: hardship deferral, the payment resumes later and interest cost is not modeled" | Goes under F+P on purpose (P itself is deferred) |

Composition rule: `leverLadder` filters to available levers in order 1→2→3, applies effects **cumulatively** (`spendingAfter = max(0, shockedSpending + Σ deltas)`; the `max(0, ...)` is a defensive guard, asserted unreachable on all fixtures), and re-runs `shocks.runway(bufferCents, oneOffCents, shockedIncome, spendingAfter)` per step. Display rules for the +N column (in planText, dash clean): both finite → `"+X.X months"`; baseline finite and after `no_shortfall` → `"clears the shortfall (120+ months)"`; baseline `buffer_depleted` → `"+0.0 months (buffer depleted: restore a positive balance first)"`.

```ts

  label: string          // "1 month of spending" ... "6 months of spending (stretch)"
  amountCents: number
  monthsToReach: number  // or MONTHS_UNREACHABLE
  highlight: 'goal' | 'stretch' | 'plain'
}

export interface LeverRow {
  id: LeverId
  label: string
  caveat: string
  effectCents: number            // magnitude of the monthly spending cut
  runwayAfter: string            // formatDeciMonths(runwayAfter.deciMonths, state)
  plusLabel: string              // per display rules above
  plusDeciMonths: number         // raw, for tests
  stepDeciMonths: number         // raw, for tests
}

export interface PlanText {
  goal: string[]          // E2 lines + cut/status lines (numbers from goalPlan)
  goalChips: GoalChip[]   // milestone chips, goal block
  backup: string[]        // E2 lines + cut floor / horizon definition lines
  levers: LeverRow[]      // the ladder table rows
  definitions: string[]   // the "our definition" disclosure strip
}
// signature unchanged:
export function buildPlanText(profile, result, twist, band): PlanText

E6 judge mode and E7 Solana touch next. ## Product A financial resilience engine for real bank customers, built for the Tangerine track of the Sheridan Datathon 2026. At judging a judge picks an `account_id` and a twist card, and the engine runs live in about five minutes: 1. **Know the customer.** Any account shows typical income I, fixed costs F, spending S, savings buffer B, household bills H, loan payment P, gap, and months of runway, all from the precomputed profile artifact. 2. **Take a shock.** A shock (job loss with EI at 55 percent, bills up 15 percent, a one-off repair, or a mix) changes income or spending and the runway recomputes with the judge's branch rules. 3. **Make a plan.** A goal plan (emergency fund) and a backup plan (if the shock lands) built from the same numbers. The one-minute pitch opens with the Storm Atlas: the runway distribution across all 4,500 accounts, then one click drills into any account for the live twist. Every number a judge sees traces back to source rows through provenance checksums. The orbit game and the findings-first report framing are dropped as surfaces; their machinery may be reused internally. ## Hard constraints - **Judge definitions are the contract.** I, F, S, B, H, P and the runway come from docs/tangerine-challenge.md. Any deviation must be deliberate, documented in docs/decisions.md, and explainable to a judge. - **Integer cents end to end.** Dollars convert with `np.rint(dollars * 100)` once at load; every metric, mean, median and runway division afterwards is integer arithmetic with ROUND_HALF_UP (ties away from zero). No float may decide a branch. - **Deterministic offline artifact.** profiles.json carries no timestamps, no randomness, and no floats; two consecutive builds are byte identical. All data is bundled for an offline booth. - **Checksummed sources fail loud.** The three canonical CSVs are verified against data/tangerine/SHA256SUMS before any row is read. - **Any account must work.** All 4500 accounts, including the five edge flags (pensioner, thin history, zero income, defaulted loan, negative buffer), must render without a special case. - **One weather vocabulary.** src/lib/verdict.ts owns the five bands (critical, storm warning, watch, fair skies, clear) over integer deci months (10, 30, 60, 120). The deprecated seven-state ladder (weatherState.ts) was deleted in E5; no surface may reintroduce it. - **Honest sentences.** A sentence can never claim a twist the numbers did not run; scenario wording derives from the same Twist object the math ran (stormAtlas.shockedAtlasScenario). - **Content convention:** no em dashes, en dashes, minus signs, double hyphens, or spaced hyphens in shipped strings. verify.py scans the artifact and dashScan.test.ts scans the site strings. - **Static hosting only.** GitHub Pages, no server, no runtime network calls beyond bundled assets. ## Stack - Python 3.14 + uv + pandas + numpy for the offline engine pipeline; pytest for tests. Modules are header-style, snake_case, type hinted. - React 19, Vite 6, TypeScript 5.7 strict, Tailwind 3.4, Zustand 5, Vitest for the site. - three 0.170 + @react-three/fiber is legacy from the dropped game layer; not part of the engine surface. - GitHub Pages via GitHub Actions, base path aware. ## Phases E1 to E7 - **E1 profile precompute (COMPLETE).** scripts/engine writes public/data/engine/profiles.json (meta plus one profile per account). - **E2 console base (COMPLETE).** Account lookup, baseline card, shock presets plus sliders, verdict, plan text. - **E3 weather viz (COMPLETE).** Forecast strip, storm front, landfall pin, verdict bands, EI-cliff overlay. - **E4 plan engine (IN FLIGHT).** Goal math plus backup levers with +N months effects; golden_plans.json cross-language drift guard. - **E5 Storm Atlas (IN FLIGHT).** Population headline plus strip-plot drill-down, bank-wide scenario mode. - **E6 judge mode.** Keyboard shortcuts, edge-account guards, rehearsal, and paper fallback. - **E7 Solana A+ touch.** Gated memo package plus honest receipt badge in the verdict card. ## Data layer ``` data/tangerine/*.csv (checksums in SHA256SUMS) -> scripts/engine/load.py (verify, integer cent parse, grouping) -> scripts/engine/metrics.py (pure I, F, S, B, H, gap, flags) -> scripts/engine/shocks.py (pure runway function) -> scripts/engine/build.py (meta + profiles, deterministic) -> public/data/engine/profiles.json -> scripts/engine/verify.py (naive csv recompute, drift diff, SHA256) ``` - Sources: monthly_summary.csv (185,326 rows), loans.csv (682), accounts.csv (4,500), over 2020-01 to 2025-12. - The artifact: about 4.7 MB compact JSON, 4500 profiles, meta block with sources, definitions, checksum recipe, and edge flag counts. - Provenance: each profile carries a check_sum over `account_id:month` rows and `money_in` cents, recipe in pipeline_lib.checksum and mirrored by src/data/checksum.ts. ## Verification - `uv run python -m scripts.engine.build` and `uv run python -m scripts.engine.verify` (independent naive recompute, dash scan, SHA256, exit non zero on drift). - `uv run pytest -q`: golden fixtures pinned to both metrics.pipeline and the shipped artifact; determinism; check_sum recomputation. - `npx vitest run`: shock math pinned to golden_fixtures.json and golden_plans.json (TS and Python twins), 4500-profile cross checks, atlas conservation tests (every account exactly once, bins sum to 4500), deterministic plot jitter, headline honesty cases, dash scan. ## Frontend layering 1. **Data (src/data):** typed loaders with schema validation, checksum mirror, resolveRows. No math, no React. 2. **Core (src/lib):** pure functions only. Shock math (shocks.ts), plan math (planMath.ts), forecast (forecast.ts), verdict bands (verdict.ts), atlas counting/headline (stormAtlas.ts) and plot prep (atlasPlot.ts) live here; integer cents, never React. 3. **Views (src/components):** console (console/), weather (weather/), Storm Atlas (atlas/). Views render finished numbers; inline money math in a component is a review failure. 4. **Render:** presentation only, swappable without touching layers 1 to 3. Load once, memoize: profiles.json is fetched a single time and parsed once per session. App mounts the Atlas section above the console (id="atlas", id="console"); dot clicks route through the existing consoleStore.selectAccount, so E5 requires no store change and E6 key listeners remain the only store-adjacent E6 surface. ## Storm Atlas (E5 design, in flight) - The pitch opens with the population finding: the headline sentence quotes the share of accounts under 3.0 months of runway (critical + storm warning) at baseline, or under the live twist with a label derived from the same Twist the math ran; a comparison subline keeps the baseline number visible when a twist is live. - Five verdict-band cells show counts and whole percents; the strip plot renders every account as one dot on a six-segment axis aligned to the band edges (0-1, 1-3, 3-6, 6-12, 12-120 months, and a labeled 120+ overflow segment for the 1200 deci cap). Dot jitter is deterministic (FNV-1a over account_id). - Scenario mode runs applyTwist over all 4,500 accounts in one useMemo (about 2 to 5 ms), so the atlas re-colors live under a bank-wide shock: "if everyone gets this twist, N accounts hit critical". - Drill-down: a dot click selects that account in the console and scrolls to it; the strip is pointer-first and the console lookup is the capability-equal keyboard path. ## Performance budget - Artifact: profiles.json under 5 MB, single request, parse once; id index search under 10 ms. - Shock recalculation: integer arithmetic, under 1 ms per interaction for one account; the atlas population pass is about 2 to 5 ms per twist change inside one useMemo. - Everything bundled for offline booths; network allowed as a bonus, never a dependency. ## Gemini shock input (gated add-on, post E2) A typed-shock path where a judge's sentence maps to the shared ShockSpec (incomeFactor, billsPct, oneOffMonths, display-only duration) feeding the same Twist consumer as the presets. shockParse.ts owns the parse boundary; pendingShock never writes twist; confirmTypedShock is the single gate into state. Plain fetch to the generativelanguage.googleapis.com generateContent endpoint (no SDK, CORS), model gemini-3.5-flash-lite or 3.6-flash with thinkingLevel minimal and store false, strict JSON responseSchema. Key in import.meta.env.VITE_GEMINI_KEY, inlined, never printed. Hard 3 second AbortSignal.timeout, automatic fallback to preset cards on any failure, mode badge always shows the origin of the applied shock. Prompt payload: sentence, account_id, six baseline metrics (approved Nov 07 2026). Booth abort condition and full field ranges: see the E2-era architecture snapshot in git history and docs/decisions.md. ``` ## Ready-to-land: `docs/decisions.md` entry (append to end) ```markdown ## Nov 07 2026, Phase E5: Atlas fold onto verdict bands and the banded strip plot **Context**: the atlas scaffold counted the deprecated seven-state ladder (weatherState.ts, quarantined since E3) and had no strip-plot data, while the pitch must open with the runway distribution across all 4,500 accounts and drill into one account for the live twist. **Decision**: delete weatherState.ts and its tests outright (verdict.ts already owns labels, glyphs and thresholds; a wrapper would only re-serve them and keep dead state names alive). Reband stormAtlas.ts onto the five verdict bands; the default headline quotes under 3.0 months of runway (critical plus storm warning), and scenario wording derives from the same Twist object applyTwist runs via shockedAtlasScenario, so a sentence can never claim a twist the numbers did not run. The atlas mounts as a section above the console in App.tsx; dot clicks call the existing consoleStore.selectAccount, so E5 makes no store change and needs no E6 seam. **Rationale**: one vocabulary cannot drift; label and numbers from one twist object makes mislabeling structurally impossible; the band-aligned axis keeps the under 3 month mass legible across a 120 month range. **Trade-offs**: the researched 7-state nuances (drought ratio, negative_buffer to flood) retire in favor of the plain verdictBand answer; whole percents may not sum to 100; 4,500 SVG circles are memoized with a documented single-path fallback if a twist-drag frame exceeds 50 ms. ``` ## README wording contract (hand to the doc agent; they own README.md) The two README paragraphs (Storm Atlas section and the pipeline paragraph) should say, in the repo's voice: the atlas summarizes all 4,500 profiles into the **five verdict bands** (critical, storm warning, watch, fair skies, clear) and renders a **strip plot**: every account is one dot positioned by months of runway on an axis split at the verdict band edges with a labeled 120+ segment for the capped runway. ## QUESTIONS FOR USER
- Q1: Esc semantics conflict: `consoleStore.ts` documents "Esc clears the lookup query" while the E6 brief says "Esc = clear selection". - Q2: Rehearsal form: an in-app timed dock (small component driving the real console through 5 scripted steps) vs a printed script only (section of the paper sheet). Recommended default: in-app dock with the printed script as the named cut line if the hour runs short (the script data module ships either way).

---

## Architecture: Judge Mode (E6) - Phase 6 of 7

### Overview
E6 turns the console into a live judging instrument: one authoritative keyboard map exported from `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` and wired by a thin window-level adapter hook, an edge-account guard rebuilt to read the E1 profile flags (with contextual copy for the layoff-on-pensioner case), a lean scripted rehearsal dock over 5 frozen golden-fixture accounts, and a one-page printable judge sheet in `public/` as the laptop-dead fallback. All rules stay pure functions in `src/lib`; components only wire listeners and markup, and the adapter fires exactly one existing atomic store action per keystroke.

Out of scope: any store action changes, any shock math, any E4 plan content.

| Key registry + resolver | Single authoritative key table, pure context-aware resolution, modifier policy | `src/lib/judgeMode.ts` (rewrite) |

### Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Why | Alternative Rejected | Trade-off |
|----------|--------|-----|---------------------|-----------|
| Key map source of truth | One `JUDGE_SHORTCUTS` table in `src/lib/judgeMode.ts`; `consoleStore` comment points at it | The brief names judgeMode as owner; one table means the bar, the tests, and the sheet cannot drift | Keeping two maps with a sync comment | The E2 comment wording (Esc, arrows) is superseded; recorded in decisions.md |
| Key set | Exactly the reserved map: `1`-`4`, `r`, `Shift+R`, `/`, `Esc`, `N` (9 bindings) | Reserved map is the approved contract; arrows removed (they conflicted with the map and with text selection via Shift+arrows) | Keeping ArrowLeft/ArrowRight walking | Account browsing loses keyboard stepping; lookup typing and N cover the ritual |
| Modifier policy | Reject ctrl/meta/alt always; `shiftKey` allowed only for bindings with `allowShift` (only `Shift+R`) | Shift alone never triggers browser shortcuts; `Shift+R` needs it; `Shift+4` types `$` so numbers cannot collide | Blanket modifier reject (killed Shift+R) | Caps Lock `R` also fires reset-all; documented, harmless |
| Listener placement | Pure `resolveJudgeKey` in lib + `useJudgeShortcuts` window listener mounted in `App` | Window scope works across Atlas and console (E5 layout); pure rules unit test without DOM; layering holds | Listeners in ConsoleView (misses Atlas focus, remount churn); listeners in the store module (DOM in state layer) | One global listener must own the focus guard carefully |
| Typed-shock interplay | While `typedStatus` is `reading` or `pending`, only `Esc` resolves; text-entry focus suppresses everything except `Esc` | `applyPreset` would silently `retireTypedParse` and drop the judge's sentence chips; typing `1` in the lookup is an id digit, not a shortcut | Allowing resets during the gate | The confirm button is auto-focused (a button), so the gate-open rule is required, not just the focus rule |
| Guard source | Read `profile.flags` (E1 artifact) instead of re-deriving thresholds | E1 flags are verified field-by-field by `scripts/engine/verify.py`; kills the dead `GUARD_MIN_ROWS = 6` and its wrong message | Keeping `rowCount < 18` re-derivation in TS | Guard trusts the artifact; drift is caught by the existing engine verify, not duplicated in TS |
| Guard placement | Full messages in the judge-facing `JudgeBar` strip (operator), short chips near the verdict (`GuardChips`) | Operator needs the sentence, judges need the glance; two renders of one pure `GuardReport` via `useEdgeGuard` | Chips inside ShockPanel/PlanCard (merge risk with E4) | Chips sit under `cp-grid`, a few pixels from the badge rather than inside it |
| N picker | Pure `pickRandomAccount` with a "safe demo" pool, injectable `rng` | Never embarrasses the operator; deterministic under test and rehearsal | Uniform random over 4500 ids | Extreme accounts are unreachable via N (still typed by judges, guarded) |
| Rehearsal | Pure `rehearsal.ts` script + lean `RehearsalDock` with stopwatch | The live ritual is timing muscle memory; the data module survives the UI cut | Full game-like scoring, persistence | No history or scoring beyond a per-step green/amber/red label |
| Paper fallback | `public/judge-sheet.html`, standalone, `@media print`, linked from the runbook | Ships with Pages, prints offline, needs no build step; runbook "Offline booth" row expects everything bundled | `docs/` markdown (not printable to one page without tooling); generated PDF in repo (binary churn) | Hand-copied numbers from `golden_fixtures.json`; an optional test pins them |

### Authoritative Key Table (ships in the bar, the sheet, and the tests)

| Key | event.key | Action | Effect | Context rules |
|-----|-----------|--------|--------|---------------|
| `1` | `1` | twist preset 1 | `applyPreset('layoff')` | Suppressed in text entry and while the typed gate is open |
| `2` | `2` | twist preset 2 | `applyPreset('cost_spike')` | Same |
| `3` | `3` | twist preset 3 | `applyPreset('emergency_repair')` | Same |
| `4` | `4` | twist preset 4 | `applyPreset('combo')` | Same |
| `r` | `r` | reset twist, keep account | `resetTwist()` | Same |
| `Shift+R` | `R` | reset everything | `resetAll()` | Same; the only binding tolerating shift. Caps Lock `R` also fires it |
| `/` | `/` | focus lookup | `#account-lookup`.focus(), preventDefault (Firefox quick find) | Suppressed in text entry and while the gate is open |
| `Esc` | `Escape` | layered dismiss | gate open: `cancelTypedShock()`; else query non-empty: `setQuery('')` (+ blur); else selected or shocked: `resetAll()`; else no-op | Active everywhere, including text entry (the only key exempt from the focus guard) |
| `N` | `n` | pseudo-random account | `selectAccount(pickRandomAccount(bundle))` | Suppressed in text entry and while the gate is open; key repeat ignored |

Esc layered rule (the Q1 default): it dismisses the innermost layer first, so the operator can never lose a typed sentence to a stray keypress, and between judges two presses (or one when no query) return the console to the empty state. This supersedes the `consoleStore` comment wording.

### Guard Copy Table (no dash glyphs anywhere)

| Flag id | Fires when | Chip label | Operator message (bar) | Operator script line (rehearsal) |
|---------|-----------|------------|------------------------|----------------------------------|
| `unknown_account` | id missing or not in `bundle.byId` | unknown id | Account id is not in the loaded profile set | "That id is not in the 4,500 account index, let me retype it." |
| `pensioner` (idle) | `flags.pensioner` | pension income | Pension income account: money in is pension, not wages | "Income here is pension, so the money in line reads differently." |
| `pensioner` (layoff twist live) | `flags.pensioner && twist.jobLoss` | pension vs layoff | Layoff twist simulated against pension income: this account has no wage to lose, read the verdict as a stress test | "Good catch: this customer's income is pension, so the layoff card is a stress test on fixed income. Their real risk is bills up, not job loss." |
| `zero_income` | `flags.zero_income` | zero income | Zero income: money in is 0, so the layoff and EI framing does not apply | "Money in is zero here, so I read the shock as a spending side stress." |
| `thin_history` | `flags.thin_history` (row_count under 18, E1 definition) | thin history | Thin history: fewer than 18 monthly rows, so the baseline medians rest on a short window | "Short history, so I treat the baseline as low confidence." |
| `negative_buffer` | `flags.negative_buffer` | negative buffer | Savings buffer is below zero: the baseline already reads 0.0 months of runway | "Buffer is already below zero, so the plan is recovery first." |
| `defaulted_loan` | `flags.defaulted_loan`, message varies on `loan.status` | defaulted loan | status D: Loan in arrears (status D): the account still pays a loan it is behind on. status B: Loan defaulted and closed (status B): no payment runs, so the loan levers do not apply | D: "This loan is running and in arrears, so deferral is exactly the intervention." B: "This loan already defaulted and closed, so there is no payment to defer." |
| `no_loan` | `loan_payment_cents === 0` | no loan | No running loan payment: the loan deferral lever does not apply | "No loan payment here, so I skip the loan lever and say why." |
| `zero_household_bills` | `household_bills_cents === 0` | zero bills | Household bills are 0: a bills shock cannot move this account | "Bills are zero here, so a rent shock cannot land; I would swap to the repair card." |

Rules: flags are advice, never gates (`selectAccount` accepts any known id regardless of flags, the hard constraint "any account must work" is untouched). Canonical order is `GUARD_FLAG_ORDER`, the pensioner message variant is decided by the live twist, and every message keeps the repo no-dash content rule (a `judgeMode.test.ts` case already scans for dash code points; keep it). This table backs the shipped `docs/devpost.md` claim: thin history, negative buffer, zero bills, and missing loans all flag before a judge finds them.

### Rehearsal Spec

Format: scripted dry run, 5 steps, timed, no stakes, driven through the real store so the operator practices the actual keystrokes. Target: 2.0 s from step reveal to "Answered" click (`REHEARSAL_TARGET_MS`); labels `fast` / `ok` / `slow` at 2 s / 4 s.

| Step | Account | Why this account | Twist | Expected flags | Expected read |
|------|---------|------------------|-------|----------------|---------------|
| 1 | `68257` | Golden fixture: odd median, running loan C, clean | `layoff` (1) | none | Fair skies 9.8 months falls to Storm warning 1.8 months |
| 2 | `23838` | Golden fixture: half cent tie in I, `no_shortfall` branch | `cost_spike` (2) | none | Verdict stays Clear, buffer absorbs |
| 3 | `98952` | Golden fixture: pensioner, no loan | `layoff` (1) | `pensioner` (layoff variant), `no_loan` | Stress-test framing, loan lever skipped |
| 4 | `49900` | Golden fixture: thin history (17 rows) and zero income | `combo` (4) | `thin_history`, `zero_income` | Caveat spoken before the number |
| 5 | `42988` | Golden fixture: defaulted loan status D, negative buffer | `emergency_repair` (3) | `defaulted_loan` (D variant), `negative_buffer` | Baseline already 0.0, recovery plan |

Coverage: all five E1 flags fire at least once, all four presets fire once except `layoff` (twice, needed for the pensioner variant), every runway branch appears across the fixtures. Candidate selection criteria (recorded for any future re-pick): ids come from `scripts/engine/golden_fixtures.json`, which is hand-verified and pinned by both pytest and vitest; `rehearsal.test.ts` asserts each step's id exists in the shipped `profiles.json` with exactly the expected flags, so artifact drift fails a test and names the step. If a rebuild ever invalidates an id, re-pick from `meta.edge_flag_counts` smallest buckets first (`zero_income` 14, `negative_buffer` 23, `defaulted_loan` 45, `thin_history` 377, `pensioner` 740), preferring fixture-frozen ids so the paper sheet example stays pinned.

UI (`RehearsalDock`): opened from a toggle in `JudgeBar`; shows step n of 5, the judge card sentence (from `presetById`), the script line, a "Run step" button (selects the account and applies the preset via the store), and an "Answered" button that stops the stopwatch and prints the verdict label. Closing resets the counter. No persistence, no network, no score history.

Cut line (Q2 default): if the hour runs short, cut `RehearsalDock.tsx` and keep `rehearsal.ts` plus a printed script block in the judge sheet. The data module is cheap and the sheet prints it.
